text:
chen: Hey—saw a p99 spike on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate yesterday evening around the 20:00 UTC window. Looks correlated with a routing policy rollout. :eyes:

mona: Which dashboard? can you paste the link?

chen: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/latency?endpoint=/v1/generate — p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~520ms. p50/p95 stable.

ryan: If p50/p95 are stable and p99 moves, likely a small tail cohort. Could be a specific client or a model-variant fallback. Did the routing policy change route weights or add a new variant?

chen: The policy switch was to route a subset to "low-cost-quant" variant when model load > 70%. It was enabled by weights: 95% main, 5% quant. No canary.

sara: 5% can still affect p99. We need to know: are p99s attributed by final route or original route? dashboards currently tag by final backend route, IIRC.

mona: Right — attribution is confusing. Our rollup pipeline attaches route tags after routing decision, so metrics reflect backend variant, not the policy that selected it. That makes the console route breakdown mislead when investigating policy regressions.

ryan: Can we quickly check the raw event samples for that window? query below:
```
SELECT route, client_id, cache_hit, latency_ms
FROM telemetry.span_samples
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate' AND ts BETWEEN 3580998000 AND 3581002400
ORDER BY latency_ms DESC
LIMIT 200
```

chen: I ran a small sample. Top 20 p99 offenders were almost entirely cache_miss + route="low-cost-quant" and 3 different client_ids showed up repeatedly.

sara: So two issues: attribution (metric shows backend route, not selecting policy) and sampling bias (small client cohort hitting quant variant). For correctness we probably need a composite tag: policy_id + backend_variant.

mona: Agreed. UX on the dashboard should show both "selected_policy" and "backend_variant" in the endpoint breakdown. Otherwise pctl by route is misleading for rollouts.

ryan: Short-term mitigation: add an overlay that shows p99 when filtered by selected_policy. Quick patch: add a derived tag in the telemetry pipeline — copy policy_id into the metric labels before rollup. That gives immediate visibility without changing rollup semantics.

opsbot: deploy:telemetry-pipeline v2026.3.8 deployed to staging at 3581002100 :rocket: 

mona: Long-term we should document what p50/p95/p99 semantics are: pctl over final latencies with labels set at decision-time vs after-backend. Docs + the UI help text.

sara: Also we should ensure the console percentile calc uses stable bucketing (we use TDigest) and that sample counts are surfaced next to percentiles — helps determine if p99 is from few samples.

chen: Action items: 1) patch telemetry to copy policy_id into labels (ryan) 2) add selected_policy filter overlay on dashboard (mona) 3) doc blurb about attribution semantics + sample counts (sara) 4) follow up on client_ids to notify support (chen).

ryan: I'll open a tiny PR for the pipeline patch and include the query I used + sample CSV.

mona: I'll do the dashboard overlay tomorrow morning.

sara: I'll write the doc blurb and add a short note on TDigest limits for tiny sample counts.

chen: Thanks. If anyone hits the same spike, check the sample_count column in the tooltips — that'll save debugging cycles. :thumbsup:

mona: 👍

ryan: on it :zap:
